# New-ZbxMapLink

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a map link for the -Link of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxMapLink [-IndicatorType <ZabbixMapIndicatorType>] [-ItemId <ulong>] [-Element1Id <ulong>] [-Element2Id <ulong>] [-Label <string>] [-ShowLabel <ZabbixMapShowElementLabel>] [-DrawType <ZabbixDrawType>] [-Color <string>] [-LinkTrigger <ZabbixMapLinkTriggerRequest[]>] [-Threshold <ZabbixMapLinkThresholdRequest[]>] [-Highlight <ZabbixMapLinkHighlightRequest[]>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A link joins two map elements and can change its color while a trigger is in the problem state. The New-ZbxMapLink cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Link of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap take as it is, alone or in an array. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Link two elements of a map

```powershell
$router, $switch = (Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectElements).Elements
$uplink = New-ZbxMapLink -Element1Id $router.MapElementId -Element2Id $switch.MapElementId -Label 'uplink' -Color '00AA00'
$null = Set-ZbxMap -InputObject 'Office map' -Link $uplink
(Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectLinks).Links | Format-Table LinkId, Color, DrawType
```

The builder writes one link hashtable between two element ids (-Element1Id/-Element2Id, read with Get-ZbxMap -SelectElements); Set-ZbxMap -Link replaces the map's links with it.

### Example 2: Draw a link as a dashed line

```powershell
$router, $switch = (Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectElements).Elements
$uplink = New-ZbxMapLink -Element1Id $router.MapElementId -Element2Id $switch.MapElementId -Label 'backup' -Color 'CC0000' -DrawType DashedLine
$null = Set-ZbxMap -InputObject 'Office map' -Link $uplink
(Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectLinks).Links | Format-Table LinkId, Color, DrawType
```

-DrawType picks the line style (Line, BoldLine, Dot, DashedLine ...); -Link replaces the previous link.
